question.text:
An antique broker has records about the value of an artwork $y$ (in thousands of dollars) at certain times $t$ (in decades) since the artwork was produced. The scatter plot for the data and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above.

According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted datapoint?
question.explanation:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

\[ \textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \]

The highlighted datapoint has coordinates $(4,35).$ So, our actual value is $y=35.$

On the other hand, the point on the regression line that corresponds to $x=4$ has the $y$-coordinate $40.$ So, our estimated value is $\widehat{y}=40.$

As a result,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Residual} &= \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \\[3pt] &= y-\widehat{y} \\[3pt] &= 35-40 \\[3pt] &= -5. \end{align*}

Therefore, the residual is $\$(-5\,000).$

question.text:
An antique broker has records about the value of an artwork $y$ (in thousands of dollars) at certain times $t$ (in decades) since the artwork was produced. The residual plot above was constructed after fitting a linear regression model on this data set. Which of the following statements are true?

  1. When $t=5,$ the regression equation underestimates the value of $y.$
  2. The residuals appear randomly scattered about the horizontal axis (there are no obvious trends).
  3. This linear regression is probably a good fit for the data.
question.explanation:
Let's examine the statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true. The residual equals the actual value minus the estimated value: \[ \textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \] From the plot, the residual at $t=5$ is positive. So, we have that $\text{Actual} > \textrm{Estimated},$ and therefore the model underestimates this data point.

  • Statement II is false. The plot shows the residuals tend to grow as time increases. So, there is a trend, as shown below.

  • Statement III is false. Since the residuals are not randomly scattered above and below the horizontal axis, our regression line is not a good fit for the given data.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

question.text:
An employee of a car dealership collects data on the value $y$ (in thousands of dollars) of a particular car model $x$ years after its release to the market. The scatter plot for the data and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above.

According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted datapoint?
question.explanation:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

\[ \textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \]

The highlighted datapoint has coordinates $(6,12).$ So, our actual value is $y=12.$

On the other hand, the point on the regression line that corresponds to $x=6$ has the $y$-coordinate $10.$ So, our estimated value is $\widehat{y}=10.$

As a result,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Residual} &= \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \\[3pt] &= y-\widehat{y} \\[3pt] &= 12-10 \\[3pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the residual is $\$2\,000.$
